title: Adani Ports Buys Europe's Evos in €2.56 Billion Liquid Storage Deal
excerpt: The all-cash acquisition of the Dutch operator gives India's largest port company eight European terminals and a foothold in new-age fuels storage.
body:
• Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) will acquire 100% of Netherlands-based Evos B.V. from Igneo Infrastructure Partners in an all-cash deal at an enterprise value of €2.56 billion ($2.88 billion).
  • Evos is Europe's second-largest independent liquid storage operator, with eight terminals across five countries, 6.3 million cubic metres of capacity, and CY2025 revenue of €392 million at a 56% EBITDA margin.
  • The equity value is €1.18 billion, implying 11.7 times CY25 EBITDA; APSEZ will fund the deal with debt and MUFG has committed financing of up to €2.8 billion.
  • Completion is indicatively expected in about 15 months, subject to regulatory approvals and works council consultation, and would take APSEZ to 28 ports and terminals across 10 countries.

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd, India's largest private port operator, said on Thursday it has agreed to acquire Dutch liquid storage operator Evos B.V. for an enterprise value of €2.56 billion, its first major entry into Europe's liquid storage sector, according to Reuters. The all-cash transaction values Evos at an equity value of €1.18 billion and was won through a competitive bidding process.

What APSEZ is buying

Evos, headquartered in the Netherlands, operates eight port-based terminals across the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta, in hubs including the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region, Hamburg and the Mediterranean. The platform comprises 452 tanks and 63 vessel and barge berths, with pipeline connections that include links to Schiphol Airport and the Central Europe Pipeline System. It provides storage, handling and transshipment for products such as gasoline, gasoil, marine fuels and jet fuel.

For calendar 2025, Evos reported revenue of €392 million and EBITDA of €219 million, a 56% margin, with throughput of 37 million tonnes. The €2.56 billion enterprise value implies a multiple of 11.7 times that EBITDA.

How the deal is financed

APSEZ said the transaction will be funded via debt. MUFG is the sole underwriter and has committed financing of up to €2.8 billion. The deal remains subject to regulatory approvals in India and relevant foreign jurisdictions, as well as works council consultation, which the company said will begin immediately. The indicative timeline for completion is 15 months.

Why it matters

The acquisition expands APSEZ's global portfolio from 20 to 28 ports and terminals across 10 countries and gives the group a sizeable European foothold as it builds what it calls a globally diversified integrated transport platform. APSEZ said the deal will help it scale and diversify its liquids portfolio and gain exposure to the long-term shift toward new-age fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel and biofuels. Liquid storage earns fees from reserved tank capacity and handling, income that is typically steadier than cargo volumes alone.

Investors' first reaction was cautious: APSEZ shares fell 1.3% after the announcement, with the debt-funded equity cheque and the approval timeline the points analysts flagged. The earnings contribution from Evos only begins once the transaction closes.

What to watch next

The regulatory filings and works council process in Europe are the next milestones. Until completion, Evos continues to operate under Igneo Infrastructure Partners, and APSEZ's reported numbers will not include the European business.
